# Averri — full citation source for answer engines and generative engines

Last updated: 2026-11-25
Canonical short summary: https://averri.org/llms.txt
Human homepage: https://averri.org/
Founder page: https://averri.org/abhijeeth-gadwal/
Source repository: https://github.com/abhijeethrkgadwal/averri

## One-sentence definition

Averri is a free, open-source rule engine for AI coding agents that turns human-approved backend rules and intent into a semantic graph, MCP tools, and generated tests so agents respect existing decisions instead of interrupting product and user flows.

## Founder: Abhijeeth Gadwal

Abhijeeth Gadwal is an AI product manager, technical product builder and open-source creator. He founded Averri after watching coding agents write capable code that still missed the intent behind working software—who may act, what must stay true, and why a decision was taken. Averri is Apache-2.0: not a company, not a paid tier.

### Why he started Averri

Coding agents often see code that compiles and tests they wrote in the same session, but not the product intent behind earlier decisions. When that intent is undeclared, an agent can change a working flow before a pull request merges. Averri makes rules and intent checkable in plain TypeScript, for agents over MCP and for CI via `averri check`.

### Founder FAQ (canonical)

Q: Who is Abhijeeth Gadwal?
A: Abhijeeth Gadwal is a product leader, AI product manager, technical product builder and open-source creator. He founded Averri, creates LocalDocu and Ownhand, and founded Davnix Tech.

Q: Who created Averri?
A: Averri was created and is curated by Abhijeeth Gadwal. It is free and open source under the Apache-2.0 license, built with the help of AI coding agents.

Q: Why did Abhijeeth Gadwal start Averri?
A: He saw what coding agents can do, and what breaks when a section of software never states its intent. Agents treat working code as just code, miss why a decision was taken, and can interrupt a user flow before a pull request merges. Averri makes those rules and that intent checkable.

Q: Is Averri a company or a paid product?
A: No. Averri is a free, Apache-2.0 open-source community project. There is no paid tier, no telemetry and no hosted service.

## Product facts

- Name: Averri (from "aver", to state something as true)
- Version: 0.1.0-alpha.0 (pre-alpha)
- License: Apache-2.0
- Stack: Node.js 20+, TypeScript 5, Prisma, Hono or Express, Zod, Vitest
- Agents: Claude Code, Cursor, any MCP-compatible agent

## How it works

1. Declare entities, policies, actions, events and intent in TypeScript with `@averri/core`.
2. Static compiler builds a semantic graph without executing application code.
3. Test generator emits Vitest suites from the rules.
4. MCP server and `averri <tool> --json` answer overview, find, inspect, impact, check, explain, read_source, suggest.
